164-task model pass@1 comparison

Two 14B coding models took the same 164 code-completion tasks through the same harness, with one greedy try at each task.

Measured model comparison28 August 2026

Share of tasks passed on the first try. The scale starts at zero.

0%25%50%75%100%

Base Qwen 14B

141 of 164 tasks passed

85.98%

Flywheel 14B

136 of 164 tasks passed

82.93%

Where the two models split

Each square is one task. Its left half is filled when Base Qwen 14B passed it, its right half when Flywheel 14B passed it.

  • 127 both models passed
  • 14 only Base Qwen 14B passed
  • 9 only Flywheel 14B passed
  • 14 both models failed

A gap this small can be chance: the two models split on 23 of the 164 tasks, 14 for Base Qwen 14B and 9 for Flywheel 14B. It covers one 164-task code-completion suite and does not measure agentic tool use or general coding quality.

How we know: the comparison
Does not prove
This result does not show a statistically significant improvement, general coding superiority, agentic reliability, production readiness, or independent validation.
Limits
The base artifact digest is not pinned in this result file. The result covers one 164-task code-completion suite and does not measure agentic tool use. Hardware, runtime version, latency, cost, and resource use are not recorded in this result file.
Method
Same 164 code-completion tasks, same harness, pass@1, greedy decoding, temperature 0. Each bar is the share of the 164 tasks a model passed on its first try, on a scale that starts at zero.
Test
Flywheel 14B was 3.05 percentage points lower. McNemar test on the paired outcomes: continuity-corrected χ²=0.696, p=0.404, significant at 0.05: no.
Paired outcomes
9 gains; 14 regressions; 127 both pass; 14 both fail

Cross-harness run across 5 harness roles

5 harness roles ran the same 7 tasks from the same task set. On every one of those tasks the prompt bytes and the runtime-context bytes each role received were byte-identical, so what differs between the rows is the harness and the model behind it. 11 of 35 attempts produced something a checker could read, and why the rest did not is reported beside each row rather than left inside the rate.

This is one repetition per task on one machine. Times are wall-clock medians and not a speed ranking. It is not market performance and not a quality ranking.

How we know: the run
What this does not prove
The run is one repetition per task on one machine. Nothing here is a market performance claim, a quality ranking, or a statement about a customer workload.
Limits
  • A mean over one repetition is a reading, not an estimate. No interval is reported because none is earned at this sample size.
  • Cost covers the attempts whose provider stated a cost. A role with no cost coverage is not cheaper, it is unmeasured.
  • Latency is wall clock on one machine and includes local model load time.
  • A role that never returned a readable result has no quality numbers here, which is a fact about this run and not a score of zero. Why an attempt went ungraded is reported beside it, because a malformed answer and a missing one are different failures.
  • An envelope found inside a refused answer was still refused, and no checker graded it. That it was there says the harness produced an answer, and it does not say the answer was right.
  • The graded metrics come from in-tree fixtures. They measure a harness against those tasks and not against a customer workload.
  • The run raised before sealing, so nothing ever checked that the source tree still matched the commit these rows name. The attempts each verified their own workspace, which is a narrower claim.
Method
5 harness roles ran the same 7 tasks. On every task the prompt bytes and the runtime-context bytes each role received were byte-identical. Each square in the chart is one attempt.

headings: McKibben frozen formula is untestable on the open sample: 3 papers with free contraction, none with force; on those 3 the frozen ceiling over-reads and the false 45 form sits closer by .045 log

Pressure-loaded tubes sit far above tension members in fibre angle, D 26.7 against q95 14.4, but 54.74 is specific only in engineered pipes, median 54.6, where designers use it; biology ties 45 on 7 papers

Drawn images beat text by .38 and .27 on two new spatial classes and lose .40 and .48 on non-spatial ones at 20 tokens, interaction .66, but the locked verdict fails on its shuffled control at .35 and the advantage may be a token limit

Pairs absent against neighbours fill at .24 by 2025 against .05 for random empties, but blind raters called 191 of 200 plain chance, so a class of taboo, instrument, impossibility or vocabulary could not be tested on a random vocabulary, gain -.004

Route search over a 52 card mechanism graph supports no new architecture: baselines rank top 3 in 6 of 6 jobs and in 6 of 6 under shuffled costs, the one cost winner is an accounting artefact, and 81 percent of energy links and 62 percent of signal links have no known cost

Interface properties did not beat node properties in predicting a hidden link under BH: delta -.065 and +.028 overall, +.027 and +.085 cross region, q .55 to .74, with the independent cross region arm the one worth a retest

Hidden mechanism links are recovered by word matching as well as by typed structure: AUC .76 and .85 for words against .78 and .81 for structure on 50 cards, with planted .99 and shuffled .56, so the atlas earns no link suggester yet
An interface beam stem model overshoots Petersen 1995 by 3.45 times, 72 against 21 percent, gives CoCr over Ti 1.11, and at a fixed femur predicts a diameter correlation that was not reported

H23 fails by its own kill: a first passage skeleton is all xylem, stretched water and cold atoms share. Xylem steepness 6 to 8 against water 88, classical limit 55 times P50 with barrier 1.3e5 kT, and a false fibre Weibull map sits inside xylem's range, so shape can't name nucleation; time dependence would, and no open data has it

items.body_html:
Experiments

Each study here was written down and locked before it ran, and is reported with whatever it found. Nulls stay on the record. 90 studies have cleared review so far, newest first, and more join as they clear. Every study cleared so far came back null or went against its own forecast, and each card says which.

Each card keeps its number in our findings ledger (F667 is the 667th finding). It gives the finding, the numbers behind it, the forecast against the outcome where the study made one, the verdict, the limits, and a Verified line saying what was checked. The full write-ups, signals and honest nulls together, are on Findings.

items.body_html:
Flywheel offline benchmark record

Six test suites ran offline, with no model connected. The first five test accountability, recovery and state handling on their own small test sets. The sixth re-reads saved per-task results from two models: a base model and Flywheel Local Coder 14B, the same model after continued pretraining, meaning further training on new text.

Offline benchmark record3 September 2026

We ran no other coding harness for this record, so this page ranks no one. The full record below lists what the public documentation of Codex, Cursor and Claude Code declares, as read on 3 September 2026.

  • 95% interval: the range likely to hold the true score, with its low end named

The one comparison between two models

Flywheel Local Coder 14B against its base model

Did further training change how well the model completes code? 164 tasks

3.05 points lower

A gap this small can be chance: of 164 tasks, 9 passed only on Flywheel Local Coder 14B and 14 passed only on the base model.

How we know: the chart
Does not prove
This record does not rank Flywheel against any other coding harness. No other harness was run to produce a single entry in the capability list, and the entries for the other tools are a dated reading of public documentation. The one comparison the record does contain is negative and sits inside its own noise.
Limits
The five 100 percent scores come from small test sets of 6 to 26 items each, and the capped lines show how wide that leaves each interval. Each suite runs offline, so none of these scores measures capability against a frontier model.
Method
Every score and count is read out of the sealed record. The capped line is a Wilson 95 percent interval, computed for this page from each suite's pass count and denominator. Accountability reports a mean score across its dimensions, so it gets no interval. The comparison sits on its own signed axis, because a drop drawn on a 0 to 100 track would look like a partial success. The model comparison re-reads per-task results the two models produced earlier. Its exact McNemar (binomial) test gives p = 0.40, and the continuity-corrected test on the model comparison page gives 0.404: 9 tasks passed only after continued pretraining and 14 passed only on the base model. The record holds no interval for that difference, so none is drawn.

What each suite asks
  • Accountability. Does an unaccountable system get a low score here? This suite scores accountability only. Pair it with a capability benchmark.
  • Governed agent. Does a workflow refuse an action above its allowed level?
  • Agent recovery. After an injected fault, does the agent recover without failing quietly?
  • Provider swap. Does saved state survive a switch to another model provider?
  • Source-mined checks. Do checks drawn from source datasets still hold against those datasets?
  • Flywheel Local Coder 14B against its base model. Did further training change how well the model completes code? Continued pretraining on the workspace corpus brought no improvement in general code completion and no significant harm. The point estimate is a small drop inside the noise. The model names in these results no longer point to any model on a current roster, so the exact weights behind each arm cannot be fetched again from the name alone. The per-task outcomes are committed, so anyone can redo the arithmetic, but the answers cannot be generated again. Each arm ran one greedy sample per task. One sample shows the greedy output only, so it does not measure the model's range of answers. This compares base weights with continued-pretrained weights on general code completion. It does not measure Flywheel's checking harness, which is what this repository builds.

items.body_html:
In short

These are the terms this site uses often, in plain words. Each entry says what the word means here. Pages link to an entry the first time they use the word. New to the site? Start at the home page.

Terms

Agent
An AI model set up to take actions on its own, such as running code, browsing the web or sending messages, often over many steps.
AI-assisted
Written or built with help from an AI model. Pages on this site carry the label where it applies.
Benchmark
A fixed set of tasks used to compare systems. A score on one benchmark describes those tasks and no others.
Canonical dossier
One long record of one event or question, corrected in public as new facts arrive. Who Knew First is a canonical dossier.
Does not prove
A line placed under a claim that names what the evidence cannot establish.
Drift
A verdict meaning a rerun did not reproduce the recorded result. The evidence, the check or the claim changed somewhere, and the record shows where.
Evaluation
A structured test of what an AI system can do or how it behaves.
Evaluator
The person or organization that runs an evaluation. In Who Knew First, an evaluator is an outside group that tested another company's model.
Honest null
A result that found no effect, reported as found.
How we know
The fold-out section under a chart or a claim. It holds the sources, sample sizes, dates and limits behind the main text.
Incident
In Who Knew First, an event in which an AI agent crossed a boundary set by the organization that ran it or by an evaluator.
Match
A verdict meaning a rerun reproduced the recorded result exactly.
Misalignment
Behavior by an AI system that goes against what its developers intended. Companies sometimes apply the label to an incident, and Who Knew First tracks which label each company chose and how the case was handled after.
Operator
In Who Knew First, the organization that ran the model involved in an incident.
Oracle
A checker that decides pass or fail without a learned model, such as a test suite or a proof checker. Flywheel accepts an answer only after an oracle passes it.
Pass@1
The share of tasks a model solves on its first attempt.
Re-derivable
Able to be rerun by someone else, on the same evidence and with the same check, to reach the same verdict.
Receipt
A small file that records what was checked, with what evidence, and what the result was, so the check can be rerun later.
Sandbox
A closed test environment meant to keep an AI agent's actions away from real systems.
Source role
The kind of source a claim rests on, such as a company's own statement, a government report, a news report or an independent investigation. The role limits how much weight the claim can carry.
Statistically significant
Unlikely to come from chance alone, at a threshold the page states. When a difference falls short of that threshold, the data cannot show that the difference is real.
Unverifiable
A verdict meaning the record lacks something needed to rerun the check. The verdict names the missing piece.
Verdict
The result of a check. This site uses three: match, drift and unverifiable.
Wilson interval
A range around a pass rate that shows how far the rate could move by chance, given the number of tasks.
Witness
A separate program that reruns a recorded check and recomputes its fingerprint, then reports match, drift or unverifiable.

items.title: F114: How much summer warmth one tree ring remembers, measured in bits
items.description: A single Alpine tree-ring site keeps about a tenth of a bit per year about summer warmth on years it never saw, most of it in the density of its latewood. Averaging many sites buys far more than adding a measurement or one more tree past the usual replication threshold.

What this means for a reader

A single tree-ring site keeps about a tenth of a bit a year about summer warmth, and most of that sits in the density of its late wood. That ranking of density over width is old news to tree-ring scientists. What is new is one shared unit: a second measurement in the same trees, one more tree at a site and a network of sites can now be priced against each other, and the network wins by a wide margin.

Objection

Bits are a relabelling of the coefficient of efficiency, so what is new? Further: the regional gain partly reflects a smoother target, the null on the forecast that an added channel beats an added tree is underpowered, cores stand in for trees, cloud cover is interpolated, and the windows end near 1975.

What would change the call. Give the channel-against-tree test more power with wider panels and nested best-subset selection; an outside dendrochronologist's review; a band or period out of sample past 1975.

From the strongest objection recorded in our publication register.

Abstract

Tree rings hold several measurable records of each summer: the width of the ring, of its early and late wood, and the density of its wood. We put all of them on one scale, bits per year of summer climate recovered on years the model never saw, so that a new channel, a new tree and a new site can be compared directly. The data are 51 Alpine and 24 Fennoscandian sites from the International Tree-Ring Data Bank with five channels gap-free from 1901, and June to August climate from CRU TS 4.10. In the Alps, maximum latewood density kept 0.090 bits per year of summer warmth on held-out years and ring width 0.028; density beat width by 0.062 bits (95% interval 0.034 to 0.089).c1 In Fennoscandia, density beat width by 0.28 bits (0.23 to 0.33).c2 The gain from extra channels did not saturate by three: the saturation ratio was 0.25 against a forecast bound of 0.10.c5 An added channel and one more tree past an expressed population signal of 0.85 could not be told apart: the difference was 0.011 bits (-0.003 to 0.025) over 43 sites.c3 Averaging all 51 Alpine sites reconstructed summer warmth with a held-out coefficient of efficiency of 0.317, which is 0.275 bits per year.c4 At one site a ring is a narrow channel. Most of the gain comes from averaging across sites.

Introduction

Dendroclimatology, the reading of past climate from tree rings, measures several ring channelsDefinition: ring channel dendrochronology, our usage after the channel of information theory One quantity measured in every annual ring of a site's trees and kept as a yearly series: ring width, earlywood width, latewood width, minimum density or maximum latewood density. Excludes a climate variable, and a combination of several measured quantities. full definition in each annual ring. For summer temperature at cold sites, maximum latewood densityDefinition: maximum latewood density dendrochronology (densitometry) The highest wood density in the late, dense part of an annual ring, read from an X-ray image of a thin lath of the core. Excludes ring width and the mean density of the whole ring. full definition has long been the stronger channel. Grudd [3] updated the Torneträsk width and density series in northern Sweden to cover AD 500 to 2004 and reported that a reconstruction from density captures 63 to 64 percent of the year-to-year variation in summer temperature. Römer and colleagues [4] compared eleven proxies measured in the same ten pines in Greece, including width, density, stable isotopes and cell anatomy, and reported their covariance and climate signals as correlations.

Replication is the other lever. Wigley, Briffa and Jones [1] derived how well the mean of a finite number of series stands for the population, the expressed population signalDefinition: expressed population signal (EPS) dendrochronology How well the mean of k series stands for the mean of an infinite set of such series, k r over 1 plus (k minus 1) r, with r the mean correlation between series. 0.85 is the conventional threshold. Excludes a measure of how well the series track climate. full definition. A value of 0.85 became the common threshold for enough trees. Buras [2] pointed out that the original paper offered its value only as a rough guide, so 0.85 is a convention.

These comparisons use correlation, and each answers one question at a time: which channel, or how many trees. Information theory offers a unit that adds across sources and does not depend on which question is asked. The bitDefinition: bit information theory The unit of information: one bit halves the uncertainty about an outcome, so a record that keeps b bits a year narrows each year's range of possible summers by a factor of 2 to the power b, as measured by its standard deviation. Excludes a count of stored numbers, and any statement about which way the dependence runs. full definition is that unit. Searches we ran on 9 November 2026 found no study that scores tree-ring channels against climate in bits; the closest work compares channels in correlation units. A search that finds nothing is a search result, not proof that nothing exists.

This paper asks four things. How many bits per year of summer warmth, rain and sunshine survive into each ring channel? What does each added channel buy? What does each added tree buy past an expressed population signal of 0.85? Can the season be reconstructed on held-out years?

Preregistration and design

The design was written and hash-locked as a preregistrationDefinition: preregistration research method (metascience) A dated written plan for a study, fixed and hash-locked before any result is seen: the question, the data, the statistic, the controls, the forecasts and the kill conditions. Excludes a plan revised after looking at the outcome, and a protocol written only for the record after the run. full definition on 30 October 2026 at 12:18 UTC, before any ring or climate outcome was computed. Site availability had been counted before the lock without looking at outcomes: 51 Alpine and 24 Fennoscandian sites, with median series lengths of 79 and 78 years.

The locked file names the data, the targets, the filter, the three measures, the planted signals with their pass rules, the three controlsDefinition: control statistics and experimental design A version of the data with the structure under test removed (for example shuffled or pooled), scored the same way as the real data, so the real score has something to beat. Excludes a comparison with a different dataset or with a published number. full definition, the kill conditionDefinition: kill condition research method (our usage, after Popper's falsification) A rule written in the preregistration that, when met, decides against the claim with no room for judgement after the run. Excludes reasons found after the run for setting a result aside. full definition, five predictions with their rules, the multiple-testing plan and a replication on Fennoscandia by a second code path. The kill condition: the study fails if no channel carries more than the controls, that is, if the best channel does not beat the 95th percentile of all three controls or no test survives correction.

Two deviations were recorded after the lock and before any outcome was seen. The first Alpine run stopped with an error inside the isotope step because one isotope site held six missing values that the parser read as numbers. The fix keeps only finite values, so that site fails the existing gap-free rule and leaves the isotope panel, which drops to 19 sites; the failed run printed no number. The second: the Alpine check by the second code path was blocked by our run tool because a shared file changed during that fix, and it was rerun unchanged. The plan hash did not change.

Data and provenance

Rings: International Tree-Ring Data Bank chronologies for Europe [8], held by NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information as open federal data, with a request to cite the original study, landing page and access date. Five channels per site: ring width, earlywood width, latewood width, minimum density and maximum latewood density, with raw measurement files for width and density. A site entered when all five channels were gap-free from 1901 to their common end year, with at least 50 years. The Alpine box is 43.5 to 48.5 N and 5 to 17 E, and the Fennoscandian box is 58 to 71.5 N and 4 to 32 E. Most of these density sites come from the Schweingruber collection, so the series end about 1975 to 1990; the 51 Alpine windows used here run 74 to 82 years from 1901, so they end between 1974 and 1982.

Isotopes: ISONET latewood or whole-ring cellulose oxygen isotope chronologies [9], released under CC BY 4.0. 19 European sites with complete values from 1901 to 2002 were used.

Climate: CRU TS 4.10 monthly temperature, precipitation and cloud cover at 0.5 degree, 1901 to 2025 [6] [7], released under the Open Database License 1.0. Each site takes the nearest land cell with complete data. The targets are the June to August mean temperature (warmth), total precipitation (rain) and 100 minus mean cloud cover in percent (sunshine, a proxy for light).

Every channel and target series was passed through a high-pass filterDefinition: high-pass filter signal processing A filter that keeps fast variation and removes slow trends. Here each series minus a Gaussian smooth of width 10 years, which keeps roughly the 2 to 30 year band. Excludes a fixed polynomial detrend. full definition on its own window: the series minus a Gaussian smooth of width 10 years, renormalised at the edges, then scaled to zero mean and unit variance. The study therefore measures variation from 2 years to roughly 30 years.

Methods

Held-out bits

For each channel and target at a site, a linear reconstruction was fitted by block cross-validationDefinition: block cross-validation statistics and machine learning The years are split into contiguous blocks, here five. Each block in turn is held out, the model is fitted on the rest and scored on the held-out block. Excludes a score on the fitting years, and splits that scatter single years so that neighbouring years leak into the fit. full definition with five contiguous blocks. Let yt be the target in a held-out year, ft the reconstruction and mv the mean of the held-out years. The coefficient of efficiencyDefinition: coefficient of efficiency (CE) hydrology and dendroclimatology; also called the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency One minus the mean squared error of a reconstruction on held-out years divided by the variance of the true values in those years. 1 is perfect and 0 means no better than the held-out years' own mean. Excludes a correlation, which ignores bias and scale errors. full definition E is

E=1−∑t(yt−ft)2∑t(yt−mv)2(1)

and the held-out information in bits per year is

B=−12log⁡2(1−E)(2)

For a Gaussian target with variance σ2, any predictor that carries I bits of mutual informationDefinition: mutual information information theory The reduction in uncertainty about one variable from knowing another, in bits, which counts any dependence and not only linear dependence. Excludes a measure of the size of a slope or of causation. full definition has a mean squared error of at least σ22−2I. So B is a lower bound on the information the ring carries, read off held-out years. It is negative when the reconstruction does worse than the held-out mean. The network value is the mean of B over sites. Beside it we report the KSG estimatorDefinition: KSG estimator statistics and information theory The k-nearest-neighbour estimate of mutual information from samples given by Kraskov, Stoegbauer and Grassberger, here with 4 neighbours. Excludes estimates that first bin the data into histograms. full definition of mutual information [5] with 4 neighbours, and an in-sample Gaussian value from the correlation.

Channels, trees and sites

Prediction P1, density beats width: the 95% site bootstrapDefinition: site bootstrap statistics An interval made by recomputing a network mean many times on sites drawn with replacement from the panel, so the spread reflects differences between sites. Excludes an interval over years or over model refits at one site. full definition interval of the mean difference in B between maximum latewood density and ring width for warmth lies above 0, the KSG difference is positive, and density survives correction.

Prediction P2, channels saturate by three: let Mk be the mean of the network B over all subsets of k channels, and M45 the larger of M4 and M5. The saturation ratio is

R=M45−M3M3−M1(3)

and P2 passes if M3 exceeds M1 and R is at most 0.10.

Prediction P3, a channel buys more than a tree: at each site, k* is the smallest number of density series whose expressed population signal reaches 0.85,

Seps=kr1+(k−1)r(4)

with r the mean correlation between density series. The tree gain is the held-out bits of the mean of k*+1 density series minus those of k* series. The channel gain is the bits of density and width means from the same k* series minus those of density alone. Each gain is averaged over 50 random draws of series. P3 passes if at least 10 sites qualify and the site bootstrap interval of the mean difference, channel gain minus tree gain, lies above 0. Each raw series is a core and stands in for a tree.

Prediction H4, the season can be reconstructed: the site means of each channel predict the regional warmth. It passes if the cross-validated E is above 0, the reduction of errorDefinition: reduction of error (RE) dendroclimatology The same as the coefficient of efficiency, except that the reference is the mean of the calibration years, so it rewards getting a shift in mean right. Excludes a score computed on the years used to fit the model. full definition on a classic split (verify 1901 to 1930, calibrate 1931 to the end) is above 0, and E beats the 95th percentile of 1,000 phase-randomisedDefinition: phase randomisation time-series statistics, surrogate data A copy of a series with the same power spectrum and random Fourier phases, so it keeps the series' autocorrelation and loses its timing against any other series. Excludes shuffling years, which also destroys the autocorrelation. full definition composites.

Prediction H5, isotopes carry climate: at least one of warmth, rain and sunshine survives correction on B at the 19 isotope sites.

Controls, p values and correction

Three controls, 1,000 draws each, give the kill statistic's null distributionDefinition: null distribution statistics The spread of scores a control gives over many random draws. Its 95th percentile is the bar a real score must clear. Excludes a theoretical distribution assumed rather than drawn from the data. full definition: each site channel replaced by a phase-randomised copy; the years of each channel shuffled; and each channel replaced by high-passed white noise. The statistic is the largest network mean B over the 15 channel and target tests. Each test's p value comes from 1,000 phase-randomised copies of the network mean, as a p value from drawsDefinition: p value (from draws) statistics The share of control draws scoring at or above the real score, with one added to the count and to the number of draws, so it is never zero. Excludes a p value from a textbook formula that assumes a distribution. full definition:

p=k+1n+1(5)

with k the draws at or above the real value and n the draws, so the smallest possible value is 0.001. The 15 tests of each measure, and the 3 isotope tests, were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg correctionDefinition: Benjamini-Hochberg correction statistics, multiple testing A rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05. Excludes the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call. full definition at q 0.05.

Second code path

A second program, written apart and sharing no code with the first, repeats the analysis with different filters, a k-d tree KSG, normal-equation cross-validation and full-length Fourier surrogates. It ran on the Alps as a check of the code and on Fennoscandia as a replication, with the same rules and without the isotope test. The replication passes when every primary verdict matches and, for the Alpine check, the P1 effect falls inside the first path's interval. A different region may differ, and any difference is reported as a result about that region.

Controls and planted checks

The planted checkDefinition: planted check research method; called a positive control in experimental science Data built so that the right answer is known, run through the same analysis before the real data, to show that the analysis can see the effect when it is there. Excludes any check made on the real data, which cannot show what the analysis misses. full definition ran in the same job, four synthetic sites per real site, on the panel's own series lengths. A target with year-to-year persistence of 0.3 was paired with a channel at correlation 0.6, which carries 0.322 bits. The planted 0.322 bits read 0.331 by the Gaussian value, 0.308 by KSG and 0.269 on held-out years.c6 The held-out reading falls short of the truth, as a lower bound should, and inside the preregistered range. A second independent channel worth 0.222 bits more added 0.201 on held-out years. A white-noise channel scored -0.050 and a near-copy of the first channel added -0.012, so neither was mistaken for signal. Every anchor rule held.

c6 observed, evidence for claim 6
The numbers in claim 6
0.322; 0.331; 0.308; 0.269 matches the result file, 2026-11-09
Chart 1

On the real data the best test scored 0.095 bits, sunshine from maximum latewood density, against control 95th percentiles of -0.014 (phase), -0.017 (shuffle) and -0.017 (white noise), each with p 0.001. Of the 15 channel and target tests, 14 survived correction on held-out bits and 9 on KSG. Six of those 14 have negative held-out bits (the lowest is earlywood width for sunshine at -0.043): they score above the controls and still forecast worse than the held-out mean, so surviving the correction is not the same as carrying signal. The kill condition did not fire.

Results

One channel at a time

Table 1 and Figure 1 give the held-out bits of every channel in the Alps. In the Alps, maximum latewood density kept 0.090 bits per year of summer warmth on held-out years and ring width 0.028; density beat width by 0.062 bits (95% interval 0.034 to 0.089).c1 The KSG difference was 0.067. Density also carried 0.080 bits about rain and 0.095 about sunshine. Earlywood width and minimum density carried little or nothing on held-out years.

More channels

The gain from extra channels did not saturate by three: the saturation ratio was 0.25 against a forecast bound of 0.10.c5 The mean over subsets of each size ran 0.029, 0.060, 0.080, 0.088 and 0.092 bits for one to five channels, so P2 failed. The mean over subsets mixes two things: which channel is chosen and how many. The best subset of each size, which we did not preregister, peaked at three channels (0.117 bits, ring width, latewood width and density) and fell to 0.092 with all five. With about 80 summers per site, more than three channels overfit. Figure 2 shows both curves.

A channel or a tree

An added channel and one more tree past an expressed population signal of 0.85 could not be told apart: the difference was 0.011 bits (-0.003 to 0.025) over 43 sites.c3 The added channel gained 0.014 bits and the added tree 0.004. The median site needed 5 density series to reach 0.85. P3 failed, and its null is inconclusive: the interval is wide compared with both gains. Read as a curve, the held-out bits of density means rose from 0.044 with one series to 0.099 with 12, at the 29 sites that had 12 series.

Many sites

Averaging all 51 Alpine sites reconstructed summer warmth with a held-out coefficient of efficiency of 0.317, which is 0.275 bits per year.c4 The reduction of error on the classic split was 0.391, and the phase-randomised composites' 95th percentile was 0.023, so H4 passed. The regional means reached 0.217 bits for rain and 0.168 for sunshine. By month, the five regional channels together gave held-out efficiencies of -0.03 in April, -0.06 in May, 0.17 in June, 0.16 in July and 0.27 in both August and September. Density alone gave 0.31 in August and 0.33 in September.

Isotopes

At the 19 European isotope sites, oxygen isotopes carried 0.052 bits of warmth, 0.102 of rain and 0.110 of sunshine on held-out years, and all three survived correction, so H5 passed.

The second code path and Fennoscandia

Table 2 and Figure 3 set the two code paths and the two regions side by side. On the Alps the second path gave the same six verdicts, and its P1 effect of 0.062 (0.035 to 0.089) sits inside the first path's interval. In Fennoscandia, density beat width by 0.28 bits (0.23 to 0.33).c2 That is outside the Alpine interval: the same sign and a larger effect at the cold northern tree line. Regional warmth there was reconstructed with a held-out efficiency of 0.72, which is 0.93 bits. P2 and P3 failed in Fennoscandia as well. Maximum latewood density kept 0.24 bits about warmth there and -0.08 about sunshine, while in the Alps it kept about as much about sunshine (0.095) as about w

items.title: F132: Transfer entropy could not tell which way climate and tree rings are linked
items.description: Summer warmth drives tree growth, with no meaningful effect the other way, so tree rings make a clean test for tools that claim to read causal direction from data. A standard transfer entropy estimator failed that test on 135 sites, including on synthetic data where we planted the true direction ourselves.

What this means for a reader

When a study reports that one yearly record drives another because transfer entropy is larger in one direction, ask whether the method was first run on a case where the direction is known. On short, noisy annual records like tree rings, this standard estimator could not tell the right direction from the wrong one, even when we built the right answer into the data ourselves.

Objection

Power is low at about 78 years and a ring-temperature correlation near 0.2. This is a failure on short annual series. A longer or monthly design might behave differently.

What would change the call. A longer-series or monthly design with the planted check at the real coupling strength; a test of a direction statistic on synthetic data under a new preregistration.

From the paper's first stated limitation; our register records no separate objection.

Abstract

Transfer entropy is widely used to read which of two time series drives the other. Tree rings give a case where the answer is known: summer warmth shapes the ring laid down that year, and the ring has no meaningful effect on the following summer. We ran a nearest-neighbour transfer entropy estimator on 135 ring-width chronologies from the International Tree-Ring Data Bank, about 78 years each, against June to August temperature, under a plan hash-locked before any estimate on real data. On real data the estimator detected climate to ring at 15.6 percent of sites (8.8 to 26.2) and ring to climate at 11.9 percent (4.9 to 22.5), above the 10 percent reverse limit fixed in advance.c1 Read backwards in time, the same series gave 19.3 and 22.2 percent, so the estimator was reading no arrow of time.c3 With a climate-to-ring coupling planted in synthetic rings, the false direction ranked at or above the true one at 52.6 percent of sites at the real coupling strength and at 40.0 percent with strong coupling, where direction accuracy reached 0.600 against the 0.8 required.c2 The estimator detected coupling and misread its direction. It gets no direction-reading status for this kind of data.

Introduction

Schreiber [1] introduced transfer entropyDefinition: transfer entropy information theory (Schreiber 2000) The information, in bits, that the past of one series adds about the next value of a second series beyond what the second series' own past already gives. A larger value one way than the other is commonly read as the direction of influence. Excludes plain correlation or mutual information, which are the same in both directions, and any proof of a physical cause. full definition as a measure that separates information exchanged between two systems from information they share through common history, and showed that it can tell a driving element from a responding one. It is now used in climate, ecology, neuroscience and finance to assign a direction to a link between two series. For continuous data it is usually estimated with the nearest-neighbour method of Kraskov, Stoegbauer and Grassberger [2], in the conditional form of Frenzel and Pompe [3].

The method has known failure modes. Smirnov [4] examined spurious causalities with transfer entropy; later papers that cite that work report that the method can fail to recover preset one-way couplings and can give the wrong direction. We read Smirnov's paper only through those citing papers and its title. Runge and colleagues [6] reviewed causal inference from time series in the Earth sciences and set out the conditions under which such methods can be trusted. Sugihara and colleagues [5] proposed convergent cross mappingDefinition: convergent cross mapping nonlinear dynamics and ecology (Sugihara and colleagues 2012) A test that rebuilds the state of one series from its own lagged values and asks how well that rebuilt state predicts the other series. The driven series is expected to predict the driver. Excludes regression of one series on the lagged values of the other. full definition as a direction test for weakly coupled ecological systems, and we ran it beside transfer entropy as a second probe.

What a user of these methods needs is a known-answer testDefinition: known-answer test measurement and method validation A test of a method on a case where the true answer is fixed by physics or by construction, so that any wrong reading is a fault of the method. Excludes agreement with another method, which can share the same fault. full definition on data like their own. Annual tree rings and summer temperature give one. Summer warmth shapes ring width at cold sites, and a ring cannot set the weather. Our searches, run on 9 November 2026, found general studies of transfer entropy direction failure and no planted-direction test on ring-width data. That is a search result, not proof that none exists.

Preregistration and design

The plan was written as a preregistrationDefinition: preregistration research method (metascience) A dated written plan for a study, fixed and hash-locked before any result is seen: the question, the data, the statistic, the controls, the forecasts and the kill conditions. Excludes a plan revised after looking at the outcome, and a protocol written only for the record after the run. full definition and hash-locked on 31 October 2026 at 05:19 UTC, before any transfer entropy, cross mapping or lagged statistic was computed on the real data. Before the lock the estimator was tested on synthetic autoregressive series only, and from the real data only site counts and series lengths were read.

The decision the study informs was written into the same file: may a direction instrument of this kind be used to read the direction of links between other ecological series? The rule set in advance was yes only if the as-written kill conditionDefinition: kill condition research method (our usage, after Popper's falsification) A rule written in the preregistration that, when met, decides against the claim with no room for judgement after the run. Excludes reasons found after the run for setting a result aside. full definition and the planted-truth anchor both pass, or, for a labelled variant, if the variant's kill condition and its anchor both pass. Otherwise the instrument gets no direction-reading status.

The plan forecast that lag 0 would break the test. A summer and the ring of the same year are simultaneous at annual resolution, so a same-year term carries no time order and can show as a detection in both directions. The design therefore named one variant in advance, the same test with lag 0 removed, and stated that no other variant would be tried.

Data and provenance

Rings: ring-width chronologies from the International Tree-Ring Data Bank [7], held by NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information as public data with a request to cite the contributors. A site entered if its series was gap-free from 1901 with at least 50 years. This gave 135 sites in 57 two-degree blocks: 51 in the Alps, 24 in Fennoscandia and 60 elsewhere, with series of 64 to 91 years and a median of 78.

Climate: June to August mean temperature from the nearest cell of CRU TS 4.10 [8] [9], released under the Open Database License 1.0 with attribution to the Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia. June to August precipitation was run as a secondary, descriptive target.

Both series were passed through a high-pass filterDefinition: high-pass filter signal processing A filter that keeps fast variation and removes slow trends. Here each series minus a Gaussian smooth of width 10 years. Excludes a fixed polynomial detrend. full definition, each minus a Gaussian smooth with a width of 10 years, and scaled to unit variance. The mean absolute same-year correlation between ring and temperature was 0.218.

Methods

The estimator

For a source series X and a target Y, the transfer entropy at lag l is the conditional information

TX→Y(l)=I(Yt;Xt−l|Yt−1)(1)

estimated in bits with the KSG estimator in conditional formDefinition: KSG estimator, conditional form statistics and information theory The k-nearest-neighbour estimate of information from samples given by Kraskov, Stoegbauer and Grassberger and extended to conditional information by Frenzel and Pompe, here with 4 neighbours and the maximum norm. Excludes estimates that first bin the data into histograms. full definition with k=4. It was computed at lags 0, 1, 2 and 3 on one common set of years. The site statistic is the largest of the four:

Tmax=max(T(0),T(1),T(2),T(3))(2)

Forward means climate to ring and reverse means ring to climate.

Surrogate test at each site

Each site statistic was compared with 199 iAAFT surrogatesDefinition: iAAFT surrogate time-series statistics, surrogate data A copy of a series built by repeated rounds of Fourier phase randomisation and rank reordering, so that it keeps both the original spectrum, and with it the autocorrelation, and the original set of values, while its timing against any other series is lost. Excludes a shuffle of single years, which destroys the autocorrelation. full definition of the source series, each run through the same estimator and maximised over the same lags. The p value is

p=k+1n+1(3)

with k surrogates at or above the real statistic and n=199, so the smallest possible value is 0.005. A site counts as a detection at p 0.05 or below. The detection rateDefinition: detection rate statistics, our usage The share of sites at which the score in one direction beats its own surrogates at p 0.05 or below. Excludes a rate corrected for testing 135 sites, which is reported separately. full definition of an arm is the share of its 135 sites with a detection, and its interval is a block bootstrapDefinition: block bootstrap statistics An interval made by resampling whole 2 degree blocks of sites with replacement, so that neighbouring sites that share climate move together and the interval is not too narrow. Excludes a bootstrap over single sites, and a binomial interval that treats sites as independent. full definition over the 57 two-degree blocks.

Direction accuracy

For each arm, direction accuracyDefinition: direction accuracy method validation, our usage The share of sites at which the climate-to-ring score is larger than the ring-to-climate score. 0.5 is what a coin would give. Excludes whether either score is significant. full definition is

A=mN(4)

where m is the number of sites whose forward statistic exceeds the reverse one and N=135. A coin gives 0.5.

Cross mapping

Convergent cross mapping used an embedding dimension of 3, a delay of 1 year, the full library, leave-one-out prediction and 99 iAAFT surrogates of the predicted series. It was scored with the same detection and accuracy rules.

The variant without lag 0

The preregistered variant is the same test with lag 0 removed from both directions, so eq. 2 takes the largest of lags 1 to 3 for the real data and for the surrogates. It was computed in the same run and is labelled as a variant throughout.

Controls and planted checks

Every controlDefinition: control statistics and experimental design A version of the data with the structure under test removed (for example shuffled or pooled), scored the same way as the real data, so the real score has something to beat. Excludes a comparison with a different dataset or with a published number. full definition and synthetic arm ran in the same run as the real data.

  • Far-site pairingDefinition: far-site pairing statistics, our usage A control in which each ring series is paired with the climate of a random site at least 1,000 km away, so that real coupling is removed while both series keep their own form. Excludes pairings with nearby sites, which share regional climate. full definition: 20 re-pairings in which each ring series meets the climate of a random site at least 1,000 km away, with 99 surrogates each. Its 95th percentile is the bar the real forward rate must beat.
  • Time reversalDefinition: time reversal time-series analysis The same test run on both series read backwards in time. A method that reads direction from lag order should weaken or flip. Excludes a control on coupling strength. full definition: both series read backwards. A method that reads direction from lag order should weaken or flip.
  • No coupling: independent iAAFT copies of each site's ring and climate series.
  • Shared trend: independent copies with a shared line and random walk added before the high-pass.
  • Common driver: a third iAAFT series drives both ring and climate with a squared coupling of 0.2 and no direct link.

The planted checksDefinition: planted check research method; called a positive control in experimental science Data built so that the right answer is known, run through the same analysis before the real data, to show that the analysis can see the effect when it is there. Excludes any check made on the real data, which cannot show what the analysis misses. full definition build synthetic rings with the true direction known. Each starts from an iAAFT copy St of the site's ring series and adds the site's own climate Ct:

Rt=St+aCt+0.4aCt−1(5)

At real strength, a is the site's real same-year correlation. In the strong arm the two coefficients are 0.6 and 0.3. Each synthetic arm was drawn once per site.

The planted anchor passes only if, in the strong arm, the forward rate exceeds 0.8 and direction accuracy exceeds 0.8, and if the no-coupling and shared-trend arms keep both rates at or below 0.10.

Results

Table 1 gives the detection rates and direction accuracy in every arm, and Figure 1 draws the rates with their intervals.

On real data the estimator detected climate to ring at 15.6 percent of sites (8.8 to 26.2) and ring to climate at 11.9 percent (4.9 to 22.5), above the 10 percent reverse limit fixed in advance.c1 The forward rate beat the far-site pairing, whose mean was 0.056 and 95th percentile 0.082 (p 0.048, the smallest value 20 pairings allow). The reverse rate failed the limit by a narrow margin, and its interval spans 0.10. The kill condition fired. Direction accuracy was 0.519 against a coin's 0.5.

Read backwards in time, the same series gave 19.3 and 22.2 percent, so the estimator was reading no arrow of time.c3 The mean transfer entropy at lag 0 was 0.044 bits in both directions, which fits the forecast that the same-year term carries no order.

The planted anchor failed. With a climate-to-ring coupling planted in synthetic rings, the false direction ranked at or above the true one at 52.6 percent of sites at the real coupling strength and at 40.0 percent with strong coupling, where direction accuracy reached 0.600 against the 0.8 required.c2 With strong coupling, detection rose to 0.978 forward and 0.919 reverse: the estimator saw the coupling and could not place its direction. The no-coupling arm stayed inside its limit (0.074 and 0.037). The shared-trend world produced 12.6 and 17.0 percent, above the 0.10 limit even after the high-pass.c5 The common-driver arm stayed under 0.10 (0.059 and 0.096). At a coupling near 0.2 this says more about low power than about any ability to separate a shared driver from a direct link.

Figure 2 sets direction accuracy in each arm against the coin and the required bar.

The variant without lag 0 passed on real data, 8.9 percent forward and 3.7 percent reverse, and missed the planted effect: with strong coupling it detected the forward link at 2.2 percent of sites, so its pass cannot be credited.c4 Its real forward rate beat its pairing 95th percentile of 0.060 and its accuracy was 0.533. In the planted strong arm its accuracy was 0.630, and its shared-trend rates were 0.104 both ways, just over the limit.

Convergent cross mapping pointed the wrong way on real data: 18.5 percent forward against 28.9 percent reverse, accuracy 0.319. With strong planted coupling its accuracy was 0.378.

Correcting across sites with the Benjamini-Hochberg ruleDefinition: Benjamini-Hochberg correction statistics, multiple testing A rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate, here 0.05. The adjusted value is called q. Excludes the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call. full definition left no detections on real data in any direction. With 199 surrogates the smallest p is 0.005, so the correction over 135 sites can reject only when a large share of sites sit near that floor. It did so in the strong planted arm (0.978 forward) and nowhere in the real data. Over the six preregistered family tests, the reverse rate against its nominal level (q 0.002) and both cross-mapping rates (q below 1e-7) were rejected; the forward and variant-forward rates against the pairing gave q 0.057, limited by the 20-pairing floor.

By region, Fennoscandia, where the mean same-year correlation was 0.318, gave 0.375 forward and 0.292 reverse; the Alps 0.137 both ways; other sites 0.083 and 0.033.

Table 2 sets the forecasts written before the run against the outcomes.

Discussion

The test has a known answer, and the estimator did not find it. On real data the two directions were detected at similar rates, reversing time made no difference, and when we planted the right direction the estimator ranked the wrong one at or above it at about half the sites. This is an honest nullDefinition: honest null research method (our usage) A working test that found no effect beyond a stated bound, a forecast that failed, or an error of our own found and fixed, reported with the same weight as a positive result. Excludes a void run, and a result left unpublished because it was negative. full definition: the method's failure on this kind of data, measured against a truth we built in.

Two mechanisms fit the pattern. The same-year term is symmetric, as forecast, and it dominates the estimate at these lengths. The lagged terms are small, and conditioning on the ring's own previous year can absorb a planted lag-one effect, because the previous ring already holds the previous summer. That second reading is an inference from a look after the run: real data showed mean transfer entropy at lag 1 of 0.035 bits forward and 0.002 reverse, an asymmetry in the known direction, while the planted lag-one arms showed about 0.01 or less. We did not test it.

The result agrees in kind with the general failures reported for transfer entropy [4] and with the caution of Runge and colleagues [6]. Its contribution is narrower

What this means for a reader

Modern colour negative film keeps a few percent of the information in the light that reaches it, by this estimate at most about 5 percent in its best layer. That puts a number on film that can be set beside a sensor or an eye. For anyone who emulates film grain, the sheets themselves give a measured noise curve per layer, and that curve does not grow with density the way the textbook rule says.

Objection

One maker, one aperture, and vendor curves read from printed sheets. Digitising adds its own error, which was not measured.

What would change the call. Read Shaw and Dainty; measure one stock with a spectral photon count and a lab microdensitometer.

From the paper's first stated limitation; our register records no separate objection.

Abstract

Detective quantum efficiency asks how much of the information in arriving light a detector keeps, and it puts a film, a camera sensor and an eye on one scale. We derived it for the nine colour layers of three current Kodak motion-picture stocks, 5219 (500T), 7213 (200T) and 7203 (50D), from numbers Kodak prints on its data sheets, under a preregistered plan with planted checks. Peak detective quantum efficiency across the nine layers has a median of 2.1 percent and a range of 0.57 to 4.92 percent, an upper estimate because every photon is counted at the layer's most efficient wavelength.c1 In the green layer, 500T and 200T reach 4.5 and 4.9 percent although 200T needs about twice the photons; 50D needs 15.7 times the photons of 500T and reaches 1.5 percent.c2 Siedentopf's rule, that grain variance grows with density, lost on held-out points in 9 of 9 layers, and variance falls with density overall (median power slope -0.54); because our planted variance check failed, this is description only.c3 A straight hinge in log exposure was the best held-out response form in 9 of 9 layers.c4 A single Poisson hit-threshold model does not fit.

Introduction and motivation

A film is a photon detector with a long history of measurement. The detective quantum efficiency (DQE)Definition: detective quantum efficiency (DQE) imaging science and detector physics The share of the information carried by the arriving photons that a detector's output keeps, measured as the square of its output signal-to-noise ratio divided by the square of the input's. 1 is a perfect photon counter. Excludes the plain share of photons absorbed, and the speed of a film. full definition of a detector compares the information in its output with the information in the light that arrived. Shaw introduced the photographic form of the idea in 1963 under the name equivalent quantum efficiency [2] and used it to compare the information capacity of photography with other detectors [3]. Dainty and Shaw's book on image science [4] treats DQE curves, granularity and the characteristic curve together. We found these works through searches run on 9 November 2026 and read the abstract of the second Shaw paper and the catalogue records of the others; the full texts were not read.

What a sheet gives is enough for a ceiling estimate. Kodak publishes, for each colour layer, the characteristic curveDefinition: characteristic curve photographic sensitometry; also called the H and D curve The developed optical density of a film plotted against the logarithm of the exposure it received. Excludes the film's spectral sensitivity and its grain. full definition, the rms granularityDefinition: rms granularity photographic sensitometry The standard deviation of density read through a small round aperture scanned across a uniformly exposed patch. Kodak's sheets use a 48 micrometre aperture. Excludes how grainy the image looks to a viewer, and noise measured at other apertures. full definition against density, and the spectral sensitivityDefinition: spectral sensitivity photographic sensitometry For each wavelength, the reciprocal of the exposure energy per unit area needed to reach a stated net density, here 0.2. Excludes sensitivity to white light or to a named illuminant. full definition. From the first two come the noise-equivalent quanta (NEQ)Definition: noise-equivalent quanta (NEQ) imaging science The number of photons a perfect detector would need to give the same signal-to-noise ratio as the real output. Excludes the number of photons that arrived. full definition; from the third comes the number of photons. Their ratio is the DQE. A search summary we could not trace to a primary source put the best older films near 1 percent. We found no published DQE for the VISION3 stocks; that is what our searches returned, and it does not show that none exists.

The same sheets bear on two working rules. Siedentopf's ruleDefinition: Siedentopf's rule photographic science The classic statement that the variance of density grows in proportion to the mean density, so that rms granularity grows as its square root. Excludes Selwyn's law, which concerns the size of the measuring aperture. full definition says the variance of density grows in proportion to mean density, and it is the basis of signal-dependent grain models used in film emulation; Stephenson's grain simulation states it together with Selwyn's aperture law [5]. And a Poisson threshold modelDefinition: Poisson threshold model photographic science and visual physiology A model in which each grain, or each rod cell, responds once it has absorbed at least n photons, with photon counts following Poisson statistics. N is the hit number. Excludes models in which response grows smoothly with every photon. full definition, in which a grain develops after it absorbs n photons, has been used for both grains and rod cells in the eye. The study asked whether one such model describes the response and the noise of layered colour film together.

Preregistration and design

The plan was written and hash-locked in a preregistrationDefinition: preregistration research method (metascience) A dated written plan for a study, fixed and hash-locked before any result is seen: the question, the data, the statistic, the controls, the forecasts and the kill conditions. Excludes a plan revised after looking at the outcome, and a protocol written only for the record after the run. full definition on 31 October 2026 at 06:12:46 UTC, and the run followed at 06:12:48. It names the data, the measures, the planted checksDefinition: planted check research method; called a positive control in experimental science Data built so that the right answer is known, run through the same analysis before the real data, to show that the analysis can see the effect when it is there. Excludes any check made on the real data, which cannot show what the analysis misses. full definition, two controlsDefinition: control statistics and experimental design A version of the data with the structure under test removed (for example shuffled or pooled), scored the same way as the real data, so the real score has something to beat. Excludes a comparison with a different dataset or with a published number. full definition, the forecasts and the kill conditionsDefinition: kill condition research method (our usage, after Popper's falsification) A rule written in the preregistration that, when met, decides against the claim with no room for judgement after the run. Excludes reasons found after the run for setting a result aside. full definition. The decision it informs is what the grain and response parts of our film renderer should use.

One disclosure comes from the file itself. Before the lock, the 5219 stored curves had been looked at and one hand calculation had been made for the 5219 green layer, giving a DQE of about 0.11 with assumed values of gamma and sigma. So the forecasts for 5219 were not blind. The stocks 7203 and 7213 had been looked at only for calibration.

The rules that decide each verdictDefinition: verdict research method (our usage) The pass or fail of one preregistered rule set against the run's numbers, read off by code. Excludes an interpretation written after reading the numbers. full definition were written into the run's plan before the run. Any failed planted check voids its block. The full list is in Appendix A.

Data and provenance

The data are the Kodak VISION3 technical data sheets for 5219 (500T), 7213 (200T) and 7203 (50D) [1]. The curves were digitised from the published vector sheets: for each of the blue, green and red layers, the characteristic curve, the diffuse rms granularity curve measured with a 48 micrometre aperture, and the spectral sensitivity curve at a net densityDefinition: net density photographic sensitometry Optical density above the film's base and fog, so that unexposed film reads zero. Excludes the density of the base and the fog themselves. full definition of 0.2. The curves were resampled to a grid of 0.05 in log exposure. The sheets are Kodak's copyright. This paper reports only values derived from them and redraws none of their curves.

Kodak notes that its granularity figures use a modified measuring technique. We did not correct for it.

Methods

Photons

For each layer, let S be the sheet's spectral sensitivity at the layer's peak wavelength λp, in reciprocal erg per square centimetre, at net density 0.2. The exposure that reaches net density 0.2 is 1/S, and dividing by the energy of one photon at λp gives the photon count per unit area there:

q02=λpShc(1)

with h Planck's constant and c the speed of light, converted to photons per square micrometre. Counting every photon at the most efficient wavelength makes q02 the fewest photons that could give net density 0.2, and so makes the DQE below an upper estimate.

At log exposure x, the photons inside the 48 micrometre aperture, of area A, are

Q(x)=Aq0210x−x02(2)

where x02 is the log exposure at which the curve reaches net density 0.2.

Noise-equivalent quanta and DQE

Let γ be the gammaDefinition: gamma photographic sensitometry The local slope of the characteristic curve: the change in density per unit change in log exposure. Excludes the display gamma of video and computer screens. full definition of the curve at x, taken from a smoothed derivative, and σ the rms granularity at the same point. Then

Neq=(γσln⁡10)2(3)
DQE=NeqQ(4)

Each layer's peak DQE is the largest value of eq. 4 over points with net density and gamma both above 0.05.

Grain variance

For points with net density D above 0.1, four laws for the variance σ2 were compared: Siedentopf's σ2=aD, a constant, an affine law c+aD and a quadratic. Each was scored by BICDefinition: BIC statistics; the Bayesian information criterion A model score that adds a penalty for each fitted parameter to the misfit, lower being better, so that a more flexible model must earn its extra parameters. Excludes a test on held-out data. full definition on all points and by its hold-out scoreDefinition: hold-out score statistics and machine learning The error of a model fitted on one part of the data and scored on a part it never saw. Here fitted on the lowest 70 percent of the axis and scored on the top 30 percent. Excludes an error computed on the points used to fit. full definition in log variance on the top 30 percent of density after fitting on the rest. A power slope b was fitted as

ln⁡σ2=k+bln⁡D(5)

so that Siedentopf's rule corresponds to b=1.

Response forms

Eight forms for net density against log exposure were fitted on the lowest 70 percent of the exposure axis and scored on the top 30 percent: Hill, Naka-Rushton with exponent 1, single hit, Erlang with real n, lognormal, Weibull, hingeDefinition: hinge curve fitting A response that is zero below a threshold exposure and rises in a straight line above it, here in log exposure. Excludes any form that saturates at high exposure. full definition and soft hinge. The hinge has two parameters, a threshold and a slope. BIC was reported beside the hold-out score, though the forms have different numbers of parameters.

Poisson threshold

The threshold model fits net density and log variance together, with hit number n in 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 and a lognormal spread of grain area with free width, and picks n by BIC.

Controls and planted checks

Each block had a planted check with a known answer, run through the same code.

  • DQE: synthetic single-size grains with a closed-form DQE. The pipeline came back within 11.3 percent, against a limit of 20. The DQE block stands.
  • Response forms: five planted forms at the real data's scale of noise, 12 each, were recovered 80 percent of the time on hold-out, against a limit of 50. The forms block stands.
  • Variance law: a planted affine law was chosen 70 percent of the time, against a locked requirement of 80. By the locked rule the variance verdict is voidDefinition: void research method (our usage) The verdict of a run whose planted check failed or whose sample fell below its stated minimum. It says nothing for or against the claim. Excludes a null result, which comes from a working instrument. full definition, and what we say about grain variance is description only.c5
    c5 observed, evidence for claim 5
    Chart 1
    From a data sheet to a DQE, with a planted check on each block.
    Basis
    observed: measured in this study, with a result file
    Numbers
    None in the sentence; it reads the numbers stated beside it.
  • Poisson threshold: planted hit numbers 1 and 4 were recovered every time at both grain widths, 0.5 and 2.0.

Two controls built a null distributionDefinition: null distribution statistics The spread of scores a control gives over many random draws. Its 95th percentile is the bar a real score must clear. Excludes a theoretical distribution assumed rather than drawn from the data. full definition for a statistic. Shuffling density against exposure 25 times gave a top-form share of 0.36 on average with a 95th percentile of 0.44; the real share of 1.0 is above all of them, a p value from drawsDefinition: p value (from draws) statistics The share of control draws scoring at or above the real score, with one added to the count and to the number of draws, so it is never zero. Excludes a p value from a textbook formula that assumes a distribution. full definition of 0.038, which is the smallest value 25 draws can give. Pairing one layer's slope with another layer's noise 200 times gave a mean correlation of 0.66 with a 95th percentile of 0.76; the real 0.61 sits inside it, p 0.74, so that test could not separate the layers.

The preregistration called for a Benjamini-Hochberg correctionDefinition: Benjamini-Hochberg correction statistics A rule for many tests at once: rank the p values from smallest, and reject the k smallest when the kth is no larger than k over the number of tests times the chosen false discovery rate, here 0.05. Excludes a correction for one test, and the stricter Bonferroni rule. full definition at 0.05 over the control p values. The result file does not report it. With two p values, 0.038 and 0.74, the smaller would have to be at or below 0.025 to pass, and it is not, so after the correction neither control rejects. The hinge result rests on its hold-out errors, which Figure 3 shows, more than on the shuffle.

Results

Peak detective quantum efficiency across the nine layers has a median of 2.1 percent and a range of 0.57 to 4.92 percent, an upper estimate because every photon is counted at the layer's most efficient wavelength.c1 Table 1 gives each layer and Figure 1 draws them. The peak falls low on the curve, at net density 0.06 to 0.31, in the toe.

In the green layer, 500T and 200T reach 4.5 and 4.9 percent although 200T needs about twice the photons; 50D needs 15.7 times the photons of 500T and reaches 1.5 percent.c2 The preregistered rule for "same efficiency at every speed" asked for a DQE spread of at most 3 across the three green layers while photon counts spread by 5 or more. The photon spread was 15.7 and the DQE spread 3.24, so the rule failed narrowly. Figure 2 shows the three points.

Siedentopf's rule, that grain variance grows with density, lost on held-out points in 9 of 9 layers, and variance falls with density overall (median power slope -0.54); because our planted variance check failed, this is description only.c3 The forecast slope was +0.15. The variance curves also show a hump in the toe. Our guess at a cause, untested, is the hand-off between fast and slow emulsions in a layered coating together with the colour masking couplers.

A straight hinge in log exposure was the best held-out response form in 9 of 9 layers.c4 Its median hold-out error was 0.112 in net density, and every form that saturates did worse, as Figure 3 shows. Negative stock shows no shoulder within the range a sheet covers, so a form that bends over at high exposure loses when it extrapolates. Hill's exponent, fitted anyway, had a median of 0.615, which here is the gamma in another guise.

The Poisson threshold model does not fit. On the channel the run used, the median error was 0.134 in log variance and 0.043 in density, against limits of 0.05 and 0.04. A later study of ours found that this fit passed the logarithm of the standard deviation where the model expected the logarithm of the variance. On the corrected channel the errors are 0.186 and 0.068, and the best hit number per layer changes from 1, 1, 1, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6 to 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, 1, 6, 1, 1. The verdict stands either way, and no hit number is read as a measurement.

Discussion

The DQE figures sit above the roughly 1 percent we saw quoted for older films, and the planted grains show the pipeline itself is good to about 11 percent. Counting photons at the peak wavelength pushes every value up. Two other choices move them by an amount and in a direction we did not measure: the single aperture with Kodak's modified technique, and the toe, where gamma is small, so that a small error in the digitised slope is a large share of it, and NEQ goes as the square of gamma. The order of magnitude, a few percent, is the safer reading than any one figure.

The green layers carry the clearest pattern. 500T and 200T keep the same share of the information while one needs half the light of the other. A faster film here buys speed by needing fewer photons for the same density, and it does not lose efficiency doing so. 50D breaks the pattern at 1.5 percent. One stock is not enough to say why.

For a film renderer the decision is plain. Grain should come from each layer's measured granularity against exposure, with no square-root-of-density rule, and the response of negative stock within the sheet's range needs no saturating shoulder.

The threshold result connects to a later study of ours on rod cells, which found that rods and film grain do not share one threshold model on the data available. Nothing in this paper bears on rods.

Limitations

  • One maker, one aperture, and vendor curves read from printed sheets. Digitising adds its own error, which was not measured.
  • The photon count assumes all light at the peak wavelength, so every DQE here is an upper estimate. No interval is reported for the DQE values; the planted error of 11.3 percent is the only measure of the pipeline's accuracy.
  • The variance verdict is void by our own rule. The variance results are description.
  • The Benjamini-Hochberg correction the plan called for was not run; done by hand above, neither control survives it.
  • Forecasts for 5219 were not blind, as the preregistration states.
  • Shaw's 1963 papers and Dainty and Shaw's book were not read beyond abstracts and catalogue records, and may already set these numbers in context.
  • Scoring wa

items.title: F149: Did unsupported citations about fungal networks double? It depends on the weighting
items.description: A 2023 paper reported that citations overstating the evidence for forest fungal networks roughly doubled over time. On the authors' own deposited table, their model gives about 2.2 and 2.8 times, while weighting each year by its number of citations gives about 1.8 and 1.5, and only one of the four intervals clears 1.

What this means for a reader

If you repeat that misleading citations about forest fungal networks doubled, say "rose, and about doubled on the authors' model", with the interval beside it. The rise is real inside the studies that were cited. How large it is depends on whether a year with one citation counts as much as a year with thirty, and with 18 focal studies the uncertainty stays wide either way. Nothing here bears on whether the networks exist or move resources between trees.

Objection

Rebuilt denominators with zero-rate years sharing the remainder; the definition of doubled with Fig. 3 unread; the abstract's 25 and almost 50 percent endpoints not compared.

What would change the call. Blind rerun by an independent analyst, true denominators from Karst, and a read of Fig. 3 before calling any definition theirs.

From the strongest objection recorded in our publication register.

Abstract

Karst, Jones and Hoeksema reported in 2023 that citations crediting forest fungal network studies with more than their results support had doubled in the past 25 years. That sentence is now part of a public dispute. We reran the claim on the table the authors deposited, under a plan hash-locked before the table was analysed. The table holds 268 study-year rates for 11 focal studies on network function and 7 on network structure, and no denominators, which we rebuilt from the paper's supplement. On the authors' negative binomial model, unsupported citations rose by a factor of 2.19 for network function (0.86 to 4.14) and 2.84 for network structure (1.18 to 6.62).c1 Weighted by citations, the rise was 1.77 for function (0.52 to 2.99) and 1.54 for structure (0.85 to 5.81), and neither interval excludes 1.c2 Inside individual focal studies the rate rose for both: 3.0 times for function (p 0.001) and 3.5 times for structure (p 0.009).c3 With this many focal studies, a true doubling gives an interval clear of 1 only 0.425 of the time, so an interval that includes 1 is no evidence against doubling.c4 "Doubled" fairly describes our refit of the authors' model; their own fitted curve was not available to us. Counted as a share of all citations the rise is smaller and less certain.
